name: Guinean Poulet Yassa
description: Poulet yassa, widely considered Guinea's national dish despite originating in neighboring Senegal, gets a real Guinean twist here - the marinade genuinely includes mustard alongside the lemon and onion, distinguishing it from Senegalese and Malian versions of the same dish. Real technique cooks the onions down long and slow after browning the chicken, building genuine sweetness.
steps_detailed: Marinate the chicken in the lemon juice, mustard, and garlic for at least 30 minutes, ideally overnight.
Brown the chicken in a little oil, 6-7 minutes, then set aside.
Cook the onion and bay leaf over medium-low heat, stirring often, 20-25 minutes, until deeply softened and sweet.
Return the chicken with a splash of water and simmer 15 minutes more.

name: Guinean Riz Gras
description: Riz gras, meaning 'fat rice', a rich tomato-and-meat rice dish, is a beloved Guinean one-pot meal, closely related to jollof rice and known locally by names like riz wolof.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 6-7 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and carrot, and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the rice and 1.25 cups water, cover, and simmer 18-20 minutes until tender.

name: Guinean Foutti Banane
description: Foutti banane, mashed plantain served with a savory soup, is a genuine Guinean specialty, real technique boiling the plantain until completely soft before mashing so it comes together smoothly.
steps_detailed: Boil the plantain until completely soft, 20-22 minutes, then mash smooth.
Simmer the chicken with the tomatoes and a splash of water 20-22 minutes until tender.
Serve the mashed plantain with the chicken soup spooned over.
steps: Boil the plantain until completely soft, 20-22 minutes, then mash smooth.

name: Guinean Poulet DG
description: Poulet DG, meaning 'director general chicken', combines fried chicken with plantain and vegetables in a rich tomato sauce, a beloved Guinean dish for celebrations.
steps_detailed: Brown the chicken, 8-9 minutes, then set aside.
Fry the plantain slices, 3-4 minutes per side, until caramelized, then set aside.
Cook the bell pepper, carrot, and tomatoes 8-10 minutes.
Combine the chicken and plantain with the vegetables and warm through together.

name: Guinean Maafe
description: Maafe, meat stewed in a rich peanut sauce, is a beloved dish across Guinea and the wider region, real technique whisking the peanut butter slowly to keep the sauce smooth.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter slowly with the tomatoes and a little water, add to the pot.
Add the carrot and simmer 30-35 minutes until the beef is tender.

name: Guinean Yétissé
description: Yétissé, a thick Conakry-style vegetable stew, is genuinely distinctive for using ground okra worked directly into the rice as a sauce, rather than cooking okra inside the stew itself.
steps_detailed: Simmer the chicken with the tomatoes 20-22 minutes until tender.
Cook the rice separately.
Blend the okra with a splash of water into a smooth green sauce and stir it directly into the cooked rice.
Serve the chicken stew alongside the okra-sauced rice.

name: Guinean Bissap
description: Bissap, a hibiscus drink, is a beloved Guinean beverage shared across much of West Africa, real versions sometimes flavored with real ginger or mint.
steps_detailed: Warm the hibiscus tea with the ginger 5 minutes.
Stir in the sugar until dissolved, then chill and serve over ice.

name: Guinean Attieke
description: Attiéké, fermented, granular cassava couscous, shared with Côte d'Ivoire, a common Guinean accompaniment to grilled fish.
steps_detailed: Toss the grated cassava with the salt.
Steam over simmering water 20-25 minutes, fluffing occasionally, until it takes on a light, granular texture.

name: Guinean Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed with garlic and pepper, reflecting Guinea's Atlantic coastal fishing tradition.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the garlic and jalapeño, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.
steps: Rub the fish with the garlic and jalapeño, and let sit 10 minutes.

name: Guinean Mango Stew
description: Mangué sauce, a savory-sweet cooked mango stew, is a genuine Guinean staple, using firm, slightly underripe mango that holds its shape as it simmers.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion 3-4 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and mango, and simmer 15-18 minutes until the mango softens but still holds its shape.

name: Guinean Beignets
description: Beignets, sweet fried dough balls, a beloved Guinean breakfast snack shared across much of West Africa.
steps_detailed: Whisk the flour, sugar, and baking powder with water into a thick batter.
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil and fry, turning, 4-5 minutes, until deeply golden.

name: Guinean Beef and Vegetable Stew
description: A simple, hearty beef and vegetable stew, common Guinean home cooking, real technique browning the beef properly first to build real flavor.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Add the carrot, potato, and tomatoes, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.

name: Guinean Fried Sweet Potato
description: Simple fried sweet potato, a common Guinean street food, often served with a savory fish sauce alongside.
steps_detailed: Fry the sweet potato wedges, turning, 6-8 minutes, until golden and tender inside.
Season with salt while still hot.

name: Guinean Fried Plantain
description: Fried ripe plantain, a common Guinean side dish, real versions using genuinely ripe plantain for real caramelization.
steps_detailed: Fry the plantain slices in the oil, turning once, 3-4 minutes per side, until deeply caramelized and golden.

name: Guinean Coleslaw
description: A mayonnaise-dressed cabbage salad, a common Guinean side, real versions with a touch of mustard for depth.
steps_detailed: Whisk the mayonnaise and mustard together.
Toss with the cabbage and carrot until well coated.

name: Guinean Peanut Soup
description: A light peanut broth, real Guinean versions kept thinner and more soup-like than the thicker maafe stew.
steps_detailed: Cook the garlic in a little oil 30 seconds.
Whisk in the peanut butter and broth slowly, and simmer 12-15 minutes until smooth and lightly thickened.

name: Guinean Ginger Juice
description: Jus de gingembre, fresh ginger juice, is a beloved Guinean beverage, real versions steeped long enough for the ginger's real heat to come through.
steps_detailed: Steep the grated ginger in 2 cups hot water for 20 minutes.
Strain, then stir in the sugar and lemon juice, and chill before serving over ice.

name: Guinean Tomato Onion Sauce
description: A simple tomato-onion sauce base, used across many Guinean stews.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion in the oil 4-5 minutes until softened.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 12-15 minutes until thickened.
